detailed_rationale:
PVR Inox is India's largest cinema exhibition chain (355 properties, 1,763 screens, ~1.8 lakh seats across 111 cities) following the 2023 PVR-Inox merger. The business has turned the corner operationally: FY26 revenue was Rs.6,646 Cr (vs Rs.5,780 Cr FY25) and the company swung to a Rs.333 Cr net profit from a Rs.281 Cr loss in FY25, with operating margin running 29-34% across recent quarters (Jun-2026 quarter: Rs.1,622 Cr revenue, Rs.56 Cr profit, 33% OPM). This is a genuine post-pandemic/post-merger operating recovery, not a one-quarter blip.

Two earnings-quality items to flag: Q4 FY26 (Mar-2026) profit of Rs.186 Cr was boosted by an Other Income spike of Rs.244 Cr versus a typical Rs.25-50 Cr range -- a real one-off that inflates that quarter's headline number -- and FY26's tax rate normalized to 13% from negative rates in prior years, meaning loss-carryforward utilization (a deferred-tax-asset effect) is doing real work in the reported profit trajectory, not just organic operating improvement. Strip both effects and the underlying recovery is real but more modest than the full-year profit figure suggests. Return ratios remain weak in absolute terms: ROE just 3.3% (last year), -0.5% on a 3-year average, and ROCE ~7-11%. Debt/equity is elevated (~0.92), though a meaningful part of exhibition-industry leverage under current accounting standards is right-of-use lease liability for cinema properties rather than conventional borrowed debt -- a structural feature of the business model, not necessarily a solvency signal, though we have not independently confirmed the lease-vs-debt split for this filing.

Reverse-DCF: at ~30-35x earnings on a business with sub-5% trailing ROE, the multiple is pricing continued recovery, which is plausible given the operating trend, but not yet cheap. The structural risk -- OTT/streaming competition for eyeballs and a content-slate-dependent, hit-or-miss box office -- remains real and largely unpriced as a risk factor at this valuation.
recommendation_rationale: The quant Hold looks right: this is a genuinely recovering business (revenue growth, margin improvement, return to profitability) but return ratios are still weak on a clean basis and two real one-offs (Q4 other-income spike, tax-rate normalization) flatter the reported FY26 profit trajectory. Not attractive enough to argue for anything better than Hold, but the operating recovery is real enough that we do not see a case to escalate toward Sell either.
summary: PVR Inox is India's largest multiplex chain. FY26 saw a genuine return to profitability (Rs.333 Cr net profit versus a loss the year before) with operating margins in the 29-34% range, but a large one-off other-income item flattered the most recent quarterly profit print, and reported earnings still benefit from tax-loss carryforward utilization rather than being purely organic. Return on equity remains low on a clean basis. At roughly 30-35 times earnings, we see this as fairly priced for a recovering but still low-return business, and rate it a Hold.
positive_para: A genuine operational turnaround is underway: revenue up 15% YoY, operating margins holding in the high-20s to mid-30s percent range, and a swing from a Rs.281 Cr loss to a Rs.333 Cr profit at the FY26 level, with the largest exhibition footprint in the country (355 properties, 1,763 screens) giving real scale advantages in content negotiation and cost absorption.
negative_para: Clean return ratios remain weak (ROE ~3% last year, roughly flat to negative on a 3-year average) and a large part of the FY26 profit improvement traces to a one-off Other Income spike (Rs.244 Cr in Q4) and normalizing tax rates (loss-carryforward utilization) rather than pure operating leverage. The business remains structurally exposed to OTT/streaming competition for audience share and a content slate it does not control -- box-office-dependent revenue is inherently lumpy.
reverse_dcf_judgment: At ~30-35x earnings for a business with sub-5% clean ROE, the market is pricing continued operating recovery -- plausible given the trend, but not cheap, and the multiple does not obviously discount the structural OTT-competition risk to the format.
